title: Most Roman doctors admit the ban is moral—but shrink it to forbidding only absolute god-cult of images
source_text: XXV. Ac propterea longe maxima pars Doctorum scholae Romanae, commentum istud quorundam recentiorum repudiat, & fatetur ad legem moralem atque naturalem pertinere interdictum istud, Non facies tibi sculptile, nec similitudinem omnium quae in coelo sunt desuper, & quae in terra deorsum, & quae versantur in aquis sub terra: non adorabis ea, & non coles: adeoque non minus hodie Christianos, quam olim Judaeos ad ejus observationem teneri. Sed ut hodiernum imaginum cultum cum interdicto tam expresso concilient, dicunt eo solum vetari, ne quis imaginem ullam, vel picturam pro Deo habeat, eamque ceu Deum adoret, exhibens illi cultum summum & absolutum, qui uni Deo servandus est: minime vero eo prohiberi, ne quis imagines, vel Dei ipsius, vel sanctorum hominum & Angelorum colat adoratione quadam inferiori, sive relativa, qualem profitentur se deferre imaginibus, quas non propter se, sed tantum propter exemplaria colunt.
pass_a_gloss: And therefore by far the greatest part of the Doctors of the Roman school repudiates that fiction of certain more recent men, and confesses that that interdict pertains to the moral and natural law, Thou shalt not make for thyself a graven thing, nor the likeness of all things which are in heaven above, and which are on the earth beneath, and which move in the waters under the earth: thou shalt not adore them, and thou shalt not cultivate them: and accordingly that Christians today are no less bound to its observation than the Jews of old. But that they may reconcile today’s cult of images with so express an interdict, they say that by it only this is forbidden, that no one hold any image, or picture, for God, and adore it as God, exhibiting to it the highest and absolute cult, which is to be kept for the one God: but by no means is it prohibited by it that anyone cultivate images, either of God himself, or of holy men and Angels, with a certain inferior, or relative, adoration, such as they profess to pay to images, which they cultivate not on account of themselves, but only on account of the exemplars.
pass_b_english: Mainstream Rome drops Vazquez’s ceremonial dodge and owns the ban as moral for Christians.
Their new escape: the precept only bars absolute god-cult of an image—relative, inferior cult of God’s and the saints’ images supposedly survives.

lemmas.gloss: with a certain inferior, or relative, adoration

choices.why: Their narrowed target of the precept.
